title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented University of Denver traditions, from historic campus rituals to recurring student-led celebrations.

cards.title: See the DU Rose
cards.subtitle: University of Denver campus tradition
cards.notes: Look for Rosa Denvera at university functions and use the official history to connect the flower to DU’s 1912 campus story.
cards.short_summary: A distinct rose variety developed from a bush gifted to the University in 1912.
cards.evidence_claim: DU identifies the DU Rose as Rosa Denvera, developed after botanist Ira Cutler found the 1912 gift’s blossoms unlike any others; it is still used for campus functions.
cards.access_notes: Look for the rose at scheduled university functions; availability varies by event.

cards.title: Join the Founders Celebration
cards.subtitle: University of Denver community tradition
cards.notes: Check the university’s announcements for Founders Celebration lectures, forums, and gatherings that honor people who shaped DU.
cards.short_summary: A recurring commemoration of the people and vision that have influenced the University.
cards.evidence_claim: DU describes Founders Celebration as a treasured tradition dating to its earliest days, with lectures, forums, and gatherings honoring contributors to the University.
cards.access_notes: Programming and participation details vary by year; consult current university announcements.

cards.title: Watch for First Snow
cards.subtitle: University of Denver campus tradition
cards.notes: When Denver’s first snowfall arrives, check Student Affairs and CrimsonConnect for the current campus celebration details.
cards.short_summary: A DU-specific seasonal celebration tied to the first snow of the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Denver Student Affairs names First Snow among the institution’s unique campus traditions.
cards.access_notes: Occurs only when seasonal conditions and organizers support a current event; check official listings.

cards.title: Take Part in DU Homecoming
cards.subtitle: University of Denver alumni and student tradition
cards.notes: Use the official Homecoming schedule to choose a public activity, such as the Crimson Classic or an alumni-community gathering.
cards.short_summary: A DU reunion tradition that links current students, alumni, families, and the hockey program.
cards.evidence_claim: DU documents Homecoming as a tradition more than 100 years old; after football ended in 1960, Homecoming support centered on hockey and the Colorado College rivalry.
cards.access_notes: Held on scheduled Homecoming dates; event access and registration requirements vary.

cards.title: Follow Winter Carnival
cards.subtitle: DU Programming Board winter tradition
cards.notes: Review DUPB’s current Winter Carnival listing for on-campus events, then decide separately whether any mountain-weekend options fit your plans.
cards.short_summary: A week-long DU winter tradition begun in 1961, with campus programming and mountain activities.
cards.evidence_claim: DU Programming Board says Winter Carnival began in 1961 and is a week-long DU tradition, with on-campus events followed by a mountain weekend.
cards.access_notes: On-campus and mountain portions have separate current details; some mountain activities may require registration or payment.

cards.title: Plan Around May Days
cards.subtitle: DU Programming Board spring tradition
cards.notes: Check DUPB’s schedule near spring finals for the week’s campus activities and any MusicFest details before heading out.
cards.short_summary: DU’s longest-running tradition is a spring week of outdoor events and entertainment.
cards.evidence_claim: DU states that May Days dates to 1913 and is its longest-running tradition; it takes place at the end of spring quarter before finals.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled at the end of spring quarter; individual activities and access requirements vary.

cards.title: Follow Hockey Night Lights
cards.subtitle: Formerly Hockey Campout at DU
cards.notes: Watch DUPB and Athletics announcements for the current Hockey Night Lights format and ticket information before making plans.
cards.short_summary: A DU hockey-season tradition founded in 2001 and formerly called Hockey Campout.
cards.evidence_claim: DU Programming Board records that Hockey Night Lights, formerly Hockey Campout, was founded in 2001.
cards.access_notes: Format, date, and ticket eligibility are announced for each season; verify current DUPB and Athletics information.

cards.title: Track Munch Week
cards.subtitle: DU Programming Board food tradition
cards.notes: Check CrimsonConnect for the day’s Munch Week location and timing, then stop by for the listed snack distribution.
cards.short_summary: A recurring campus food week that places free snacks around DU during the academic term.
cards.evidence_claim: DU describes Munch Week as a week-long celebration with free snacks across campus; another DU guide says it occurs each quarter and is supported by local businesses.
cards.access_notes: Locations, quantities, and timing vary by current event listing; availability can be limited.

cards.title: Catch Battle of the Bands
cards.subtitle: DU Programming Board student-music tradition
cards.notes: Follow DUPB’s event listing for performers and venue, then see which student acts compete for the MusicFest opening slot.
cards.short_summary: An annual student performance competition whose winner earns a MusicFest opening opportunity.
cards.evidence_claim: DU identifies Battle of the Bands as an annual student-talent showcase; its winner earns the opportunity to open at MusicFest.
cards.access_notes: Venue, performers, and attendance details are set for each annual event; consult DUPB’s current listing.

cards.title: Recognize Profiles of Excellence
cards.subtitle: University of Denver student-to-alum tradition
cards.notes: Look for the current Profiles of Excellence program and attend or support the ceremony recognizing graduating students of color.
cards.short_summary: A long-running DU ceremony marking the transition of students of color from student to alum.
cards.evidence_claim: DU Student Affairs says Profiles of Excellence has been a campus tradition for more than 20 years and commemorates the journey of students of color from student to alum.
cards.access_notes: Ceremony timing and participation information vary annually; check Student Affairs for current details.
